title: Japan's Anime Market Hits Record $28.2 Billion
paragraphs: Spending on Japanese anime reached a record 4.45 trillion yen — about $28.2 billion — in 2025, up 15.8% from the previous year, according to new figures from the Association of Japanese Animations (AJA).

The preliminary findings of the Anime Industry Report 2026 were presented on October 30 at TIFFCOM, an entertainment industry event held as part of the Tokyo International Film Festival, with the full release expected in December.

The 4.45 trillion yen figure includes total spending on anime films, TV shows, streaming, merchandise and live events in 2025. It marks the first time the market has passed 4 trillion yen, with annual growth also reaching a record high.
Overseas sales rose 17%, while domestic sales climbed 14%. This was a big change from 2024, when overseas sales jumped 26%, but domestic growth was much slower, at just 5%.
Both domestic and overseas sales were helped by the huge success of Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba — Infinity Castle, which became the highest-grossing Japanese film of all time.
Japanese anime now also make up 100 of IMDb's top 300 user-rated animated TV series. Attack on Titan tops the list, while Death Note ranks third and One Piece ninth.

"It is no longer unusual for anime to be ranked among the top-performing box office or streaming titles overseas. It is safe to say anime has achieved a breakthrough in the international market," said Masahiro Hasegawa, the report's editor-in-chief.

As the industry continues to grow internationally, AJA says companies will need to adapt their content and business practices to different languages, cultures and laws. It also said online piracy is an important problem to address.
Japan's government has set a goal of increasing overseas anime sales to 6 trillion yen, or about $38 billion, by 2033.
